hostLatest.runStorage: TEXT36 canonical UUID matching Agent BLOB16

comparisonScope: Allocated B-tree pages including indices, not WAL file length. Long-body and multi-tool workloads are distinct; their reductions cannot be multiplied or added. Previous measurements remain unchanged.
privacy: Aggregate counts only; no conversation content, business IDs, provider IDs or credentials retained.
sampleDescription: Latest native-format five-prompt conversation, distinct from the preceding five-prompt audit; physical sizes across different conversations are not a controlled saving comparison.
formula: reduction_percent = (1 - current_bytes / baseline_bytes) * 100; a negative value means growth.
measurementNotes: This records the preceding read-only audit; it does not mutate or migrate any IDs.

Long-body data use final-space-old format1 as the original baseline, final-space-old format2 as the previous segmented baseline, and final-space-new format2 as the current baseline in the preserved C6 artifact.
Each allocation total sums allocatedBytes across every recorded dbstat structure, including indices, SQLite schema and fixed empty pages. It is not just body bytes or WAL file length.
Tool workloads use the medians of three paired old/new runs in C5; logical content digests match.
WAL logicalPageBytes are SQLite cache-write page counters, not physical I/O or temporary WAL file length.
Storage encoding is unchanged by the subsequent first-page snapshot fix. Synthetic native UUID tests already use the representation now confirmed in actual runs.
Historical TEXT IDs are intentionally retained. Provider opaque IDs, integer technical keys and the auxiliary empty run key are not UUID conversion targets.
Host app.db still stores new run UUIDs as TEXT36 and generates timestamp-prefixed thread IDs. The claim that every self-generated ID in every database is unified is false.
